answer: A registry prices each pseudonymous agent credential with a bond and a decaying reputation signal; per-epoch rewards are capped concave in bonded stake, e.g. sqrt(stake), and credentials require re-attestation at a fixed horizon. An orchard of credentials is pruned at each horizon. Attacker cost is bond plus distinct behavioral history per credential; splitting stake across N credentials pays at most sum sqrt(s_i) ≤ sqrt(total) plus fixed issuance costs, so no gain. One bond does not prove one person—only raises Sybil cost. Limitation: collusion and stolen histories.
